# #402 — SHAPE-2: Where do assertions live — issue body or a versioned repo checks file?

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: question, memory
Created: 2026-07-25T03:29:20Z
Updated: 2026-07-25T03:29:20Z

---

Parent: #400. **Question, not work. Do not implement.**

## Context

`docs/code-brain-design.md` §2 establishes that **closed does not mean
delivered**, and that the north star is not the issue text but the **assertion
the issue was supposed to make true**:

| Intent | Assertion |
|---|---|
| discards get drained | `discarded_entries` count > 0 |
| maintenance runs | `ENABLED=1` and last run recent |
| dream runs nightly | last dream run < 48h |
| files are tracked | `ob_source_files` count > 0 |
| pre-compact captures | rows with `receipt_trigger='pre-compact'` exist |

Five queries. No model, no DSL, no new format. **They would have caught all
eight wiring findings the day after each issue closed.**

The doc leaves the location open:

> *Open:* assertions on the issue body vs a versioned repo checks file. Lean
> repo-side — one thing to maintain, runs whether or not anyone remembers the
> issue exists.

## The tradeoff

**Issue body.** Assertion lives next to the intent that motivated it, so it is
obvious when writing the issue and reviewable in the same place. But it depends
on the author remembering to add it — the exact "remember to update it" failure
mode that produced all eight findings. And it needs forge API access to read,
which couples the checker to the forge.

**Repo checks file.** Versioned, reviewable, diffable, and runs whether or not
anyone remembers the issue exists. No forge coupling. But it drifts away from the
issue that motivated it, and nothing forces a new issue to add a check.

## The interesting third option

Both, with a **link**: the checks file is authoritative and each entry carries an
`issue:` reference. Then a *sixth* assertion becomes possible — **does every
closed issue in this epic have at least one check?** — which catches the
add-a-check-later failure mode instead of trusting it.

That is the shape the rest of the design already argues for: do not ask anyone to
remember; check reality on a sweep.

## What would settle it

Write the five assertions above in both shapes and see which one survives the
question *"what happens when someone files issue #401 and forgets?"*

## Depends on

#SHAPE-1 — if the checker is a separate product, repo-side is close to forced,
because it cannot assume forge credentials.
